text: Treat routing readiness as a separate condition from Case lifecycle alert eligibility. This is an architectural inference: Omni-Channel applies routing logic when work is assigned to an owner and does not reapply it after later field edits; PendingServiceRouting describes work waiting for routing or assignment. (medium confidence)
keywords: Salesforce Omni-Channel routing readiness versus Case lifecycle alerts

text: For queue-based routing, PendingServiceRouting creation does not invoke before-insert or after-insert triggers, or actions such as triggers, workflow rules, or validation that could interfere with record creation. A design that expects an insert trigger on this routing record to deliver every alert conflicts with this documented behavior. (low confidence)
keywords: Salesforce Omni-Channel routing readiness versus Case lifecycle alerts

text: The routing object's readiness flag describes readiness to route work to an agent; when true, the PendingServiceRouting record cannot be edited. This is routing readiness, not evidence that a Case lifecycle alert has been delivered. (low confidence)
keywords: Salesforce Omni-Channel routing readiness versus Case lifecycle alerts

text: In a historical Stack Exchange report, a Case user said changing Status to Open or New did not resolve the reported routing-record creation failure. This is an attributed observation, not a verified current Salesforce defect. (low confidence)
keywords: Salesforce Omni-Channel routing readiness versus Case lifecycle alerts

text: PendingServiceRouting readiness indicates whether a work item is ready to be routed to an agent; once true, the PendingServiceRouting record cannot be edited. It does not by itself attest that an agent has accepted the work. (low confidence)
keywords: Salesforce Omni-Channel routing readiness versus Case lifecycle alerts

text: Do not interpret the routing-versus-lifecycle distinction as saying that work status never affects Omni-Channel. Status-based capacity measures accepted-work status, and optional capacity checks before reopening or reassigning work can reroute work when the rep lacks capacity. (low confidence)
keywords: Salesforce Omni-Channel routing readiness versus Case lifecycle alerts

text: External-routing notifications have a routing-specific lifecycle: new work is sent to the partner application, which matches it to logged-in reps; Salesforce also notifies the partner after acceptance, decline, completion, and rep logout. These documented milestones should not be assumed to enumerate every later Case field change. (low confidence)
keywords: Salesforce Omni-Channel routing readiness versus Case lifecycle alerts
